title: A platform for nuclear symmetry-violation searches with laser-coolable molecules carrying spinful nuclei
authors: Tatsam Garg, Jakob Weiß, Tesse Tiemens, Charly Beulenkamp, Andreas Schindewolf, Tim Langen
abstract: Cold heavy molecules are promising systems for exploring nuclear $\mathcal{P}$- and $\mathcal{CP}$-violating phenomena in search of new physics beyond the Standard Model. However, most proposed experimental strategies and their early realizations to date have been limited to proof-of-principle molecular species with effectively spin-zero nuclei that are not sensitive to nuclear symmetry-violating phenomena. Here, we introduce a comprehensive experimental toolbox that integrates cooling, trapping, coherent state manipulation, and a complete precision-measurement protocol that is applicable to molecules carrying relevant nuclear spins. Using ${}^{137}$Ba${}^{19}$F and nuclear-spin-dependent parity violation (NSD-PV) as representative species and benchmark application, respectively, our approach achieves a projected statistical sensitivity roughly two orders of magnitude beyond comparable molecular beams by combining techniques already demonstrated individually in current experiments. This level of precision could provide realistic experimental access not only to the enhanced NSD-PV signals arising from the heavy ${}^{137}$Ba nucleus within this molecule but also to the contributions from the lighter ${}^{19}$F nucleus, bringing direct benchmarks of nuclear \textit{ab initio} theory within reach. We further identify a candidate magic wavelength as a route to second-scale rotational coherence in future experiments. The techniques developed here can be transferred to measurements of nuclear Schiff and magnetic quadrupole moments in molecules containing deformed nuclei, establishing a general platform for laboratory searches for nuclear symmetry violations.
summary: This paper introduces a general, high-precision experimental platform for searching for nuclear symmetry violations using laser-cooled molecules containing spinful nuclei. By leveraging techniques like Zeeman tuning near state crossings, the authors project sensitivities significantly beyond current limits. This work provides both the theoretical framework and the practical roadmap for next-generation searches for physics beyond the Standard Model in molecular systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is searching for new physics by measuring nuclear P- and CP-violating effects, such as NSD-PV, in molecular systems.
main_result: The authors propose a comprehensive experimental toolbox achieving projected sensitivities two orders of magnitude better than current molecular beam methods, applicable to various spinful molecules.
method: The method involves using external magnetic fields (Zeeman tuning) to bring opposite-parity molecular states into near-degeneracy, enhancing the measurement sensitivity via an interrogation technique like Stark-interferometry.
model_or_system: The system is laser-coolable diatomic molecules carrying spinful nuclei (e.g., ${}^{137}	ext{BaF}$). The theoretical framework involves detailed calculations of molecular Hamiltonians incorporating rotational, hyperfine, and Zeeman interactions in Hund's case ($\alpha eta S$).
key_observables: The key observable is the mixing element $ ar{W}$ (or matrix element $	ilde{C}$) derived from parity-violating couplings, measured via an asymmetry $A$ proportional to $1/\Delta$.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the magnetic field strength ($B$), the energy detuning ($\Delta$), and molecular constants like the permanent electric dipole moment (e.g., 3.17 Debye for BaF).
main_assumptions: Major assumptions include neglecting contributions from weak electric fields in certain Hamiltonians and assuming that the dominant uncertainty source is the control over the energy detuning $\Delta$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the entire experimental apparatus, from laser ablation to MOT capture. Figure 2 details the state structure of ${}^{137}	ext{BaF}$ in a magnetic field, illustrating relevant state crossings.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general physical platform and required techniques (cooling, trapping). It then applies these methods to benchmark measurements like NSD-PV using specific molecular species (${}^{137}	ext{BaF}$), detailing Hamiltonian derivations and identifying precise magnetic field locations for maximal sensitivity.
why_interesting: This work represents a sophisticated integration of quantum optics (laser cooling/trapping) with fundamental physics searches. The detailed theoretical modeling of complex molecular Hamiltonians to predict optimal measurement points is highly relevant to advanced AMO research.
